text: The property lost 25.5 ha of tree cover in 2015 due to a supported forest loss event detected by the Hansen GFC dataset. The evidence shows that this was part of historical tree-cover loss before the 2020 baseline, occurring alongside other events (0.8 ha in 2008, 4.8 ha in 2017, and 67.7 ha in 2020). The loss in 2015 was likely due to natural or anthropogenic factors like logging, wildfires, or land clearing, as the area was not classified as forest in 2020 (JRC GFC2020 confirms 0 ha of forest). No further major losses (≥0.5 ha) occurred after 2020. The exact cause isn’t specified, but the data confirms the loss as a standalone historical event.
